history.summary: One of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, counted among the earliest Chola temples; the present masonry structure was built under the Cholas (attributed to Aditya Chola, 9th century) with later expansions by the Thanjavur Nayaks in the 16th century. It is a parikara sthalam for Rahu and Kethu — Rahu is believed to have worshipped Shiva here, making it a famous Rahu sthalam of the Navagraha circuit. The main sanctum sits on a chariot-like base, and the temple is built so that sunlight falls on the sanctum only during the Tamil month of Chithirai.

name: Nageswaran Temple
town_description: Temple town in Thanjavur district on the Cauvery delta, famed for its concentration of Chola-era Shiva and Vishnu temples, the Sarangapani and Adi Kumbeswara temples, and the Mahamaham festival.

travel.railway: Kumbakonam Railway Station, ~1-2 km from the temple, on the Thanjavur-Mayiladuthurai line
travel.road: Within Kumbakonam town, near the Thanjavur highway; easily reached by bus, auto and taxi from the city bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Rahu peyarchi draws large crowds
